notes: Read all four units, full immigrant-integration context, all ten candidates and the review. Preserved the source's separate attachments: English as the official language in the nation and welcome for ethnic and linguistic diversity in the United States and territories. Restricted priority hospitality to refugees who stood with America. Identified the U.S. Armed Forces, restored explicit gratitude, and split the three civil-society recommendations with U.S.-citizenship scope. Restored the omitted characterizations of English's business, legal and cultural roles.

claims.claim_text: Support for English as the official language of the United States while welcoming ethnic and linguistic diversity in the United States and its territories.
English is characterized as the accepted language of U.S. business, commerce and legal proceedings and as an essential unifying cultural force.
Refugees who stood with the United States in dangerous times should have first claim on U.S. hospitality.
The platform expresses gratitude to thousands of new immigrants, many not yet citizens, serving in the U.S. Armed Forces.
The patriotism of new immigrants serving in the U.S. Armed Forces is characterized as inspiring.
U.S. civil-society institutions should embrace newcomers.
U.S. civil-society institutions should assist newcomers' journey to full U.S. citizenship.
U.S. civil-society institutions should help immigrant communities avoid patterns of isolation.
